kpi_name: Life expectancy, men, years
kpi_description: Life expectancy over a five-year period (the average of the year in question and the four years before it) for men registered in Sweden. For example, 2023 shows the average for 2019-2023. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Life expectancy, women, years
kpi_description: Life expectancy over a five-year period (the average of the year in question and the four years before it) for women registered in Sweden. For example, 2023 shows the average for 2019-2023. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Care Need Index (CNI), index
kpi_description: Care Need Index (CNI) uses socio-economic conditions to identify the risk of ill health. A value above 1 means a higher risk of ill health than in Sweden as a whole, and a value below 1 a lower risk. CNI is based on the following variables, weighted differently and listed here in descending order of weight: aged 65+ and living alone; born abroad (Eastern Europe, Asia, Africa and South America); unemployed or in a labour market programme, aged 16-64; single parent with children aged 17 or younger; inhabitants aged 1 or older who moved into or changed district within the municipality; inhabitants aged 25-64 with a low level of education; and inhabitants aged 0-4. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Inhabitants aged 80+, share (%)
kpi_description: Number of inhabitants aged 80 or older on 31 December divided by the total number of inhabitants on 31 December. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Inhabitants aged 65+, number
kpi_description: Number of inhabitants aged 65 or older on 31 December. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Inhabitants, total, number
kpi_description: Total number of inhabitants on 31 December. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Inhabitants aged 80+, number
kpi_description: Number of inhabitants aged 80 or older on 31 December. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Inhabitants aged 65+, share (%)
kpi_description: Number of inhabitants aged 65 or older divided by the total number of inhabitants on 31 December. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Projection, expected number of inhabitants in 10 years
kpi_description: Expected total number of inhabitants in 10 years. The projection uses the numbers of live births, deaths, people moving in and people moving out registered during the year. From these, fertility, mortality, the number of people moving in, the age distribution of people moving in and the risk of moving out are estimated by age and sex, and the estimates are then used to calculate the future numbers of births, deaths and people moving in and out. Note that the projection only uses statistics available nationally and should not be confused with the forecasts that municipalities and regions produce themselves. From 2022 the data are published every third year. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Net cost of primary care, total (excl. primary-care-affiliated home healthcare and pharmaceuticals), SEK per inhabitant
kpi_description: Net cost of primary care in total (excluding primary-care-affiliated home healthcare and the cost of pharmaceuticals covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme), divided by the number of inhabitants in the region on 31 December. Net cost means gross cost minus gross revenue. Refers to healthcare that, without restriction by disease, age or patient group, meets the population's need for basic medical treatment, nursing care, preventive work and rehabilitation, and that does not require the medical and technical resources of hospitals. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Net cost of nursing care in primary care (excl. pharmaceuticals), SEK per inhabitant
kpi_description: Net cost of nursing care (excluding the cost of pharmaceuticals covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme), divided by the number of inhabitants in the region on 31 December. Net cost means gross cost minus gross revenue. Refers to nursing care (incl. out-of-hours care), i.e. all outpatient activity, including home visits, carried out by nurses for their own patients. Covers both district nurse clinics and specialist clinics, e.g. for asthma, diabetes and hypertension patients. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Net cost of inpatient primary care (excl. pharmaceuticals), SEK per inhabitant
kpi_description: Net cost of inpatient primary care (excluding the cost of pharmaceuticals covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme), divided by the number of inhabitants in the region on 31 December. Net cost means gross cost minus gross revenue. Refers to healthcare provided to a patient admitted to the care unit. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Net cost of other primary care (excl. pharmaceuticals), SEK per inhabitant
kpi_description: Net cost of other primary care (excluding the cost of pharmaceuticals covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme), divided by the number of inhabitants in the region on 31 December. Net cost means gross cost minus gross revenue. Refers, for example, to youth clinics (including contraceptive counselling), school health services, occupational health services, podiatry, and patient information or health education for individual patients or patient groups, e.g. smoking cessation groups, weight-loss groups and parent groups. Telephone contacts with the healthcare advice line are also reported here. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Net cost of physiotherapy and occupational therapy in primary care (excl. pharmaceuticals), SEK per inhabitant
kpi_description: Net cost of physiotherapy and occupational therapy (excluding the cost of pharmaceuticals covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme), divided by the number of inhabitants in the region on 31 December. Net cost means gross cost minus gross revenue. Refers to physiotherapy and occupational therapy, covering outpatient activity including home visits and workplace visits. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Net cost of general practitioner care incl. out-of-hours services in primary care (excl. pharmaceuticals), SEK per inhabitant
kpi_description: Net cost of general practitioner care including out-of-hours services (excluding the cost of pharmaceuticals covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme), divided by the number of inhabitants in the region on 31 December. Net cost means gross cost minus gross revenue. Refers to all outpatient activity, including home visits, carried out by doctors working as specialists in general medicine. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Net cost of child health services in primary care (excl. pharmaceuticals), SEK per inhabitant
kpi_description: Net cost of child health services (excluding the cost of pharmaceuticals covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme), divided by the total number of inhabitants in the region on 31 December. Net cost means gross cost minus gross revenue. Child health services cover outpatient activity, including home visits, provided within child health care. This refers to basic, regular child health care. For some children, e.g. those born prematurely, visits and check-ups take place at paediatric clinics. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Net cost of maternal health services in primary care (excl. pharmaceuticals), SEK per inhabitant
kpi_description: Net cost of maternal health services (excluding the cost of pharmaceuticals covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme), divided by the total number of inhabitants in the region on 31 December. Net cost means gross cost minus gross revenue. Refers to outpatient activity, including home visits, provided within maternal health care. Includes gynaecological examinations, mammograms and health check-ups of pregnant women, antenatal and postnatal care, and contraceptive counselling in connection with pregnancy. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Region's purchases of primary care, total, share (%)
kpi_description: The region's purchases of primary care as a share of the net cost of primary care, excluding the cost of pharmaceuticals covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme (%). A purchase of services is payment for a public mandate (core activity) that has been handed over to another party to carry out. Net cost means gross cost minus gross revenue. Purchases of support services are included in both purchases and net cost. Source: Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Permanent monthly-paid employees in primary care, region, share (%)
kpi_description: Permanent monthly-paid employees in primary care divided by all employees in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Region-owned companies are included under their region. Source: SKR personnel statistics (November statistics).

kpi_name: Temporary monthly-paid employees in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Temporary monthly-paid employees in primary care divided by all employees in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Temporary hourly-paid employees in primary care, region, share (%)
kpi_description: Temporary hourly-paid employees in primary care divided by all employees in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Region-owned companies are included under their region. Source: SKR personnel statistics (November statistics).

kpi_name: Hours worked by temporary monthly-paid employees in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Hours worked by temporary monthly-paid employees in primary care divided by the total hours worked in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Hours worked by temporary hourly-paid employees in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Hours worked by temporary hourly-paid employees in primary care divided by the total hours worked in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Monthly-paid staff employed full time in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Full-time employed (100 % agreed employment rate) monthly-paid staff in primary care divided by all monthly-paid staff in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Monthly-paid staff employed part time (75-99 %) in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Part-time employed (75-99 % agreed employment rate) monthly-paid staff in primary care divided by all monthly-paid staff in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Monthly-paid staff employed part time (1-74 %) in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Part-time employed (1-74 % agreed employment rate) monthly-paid staff in primary care divided by all monthly-paid staff in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Monthly-paid staff working full time in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Full-time working (100 % actual employment rate) monthly-paid staff in primary care divided by all working monthly-paid staff in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Monthly-paid staff working part time (75-99 %) in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Part-time working (75-99 % actual employment rate) monthly-paid staff in primary care divided by all working monthly-paid staff in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Monthly-paid staff working part time (1-74 %) in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Part-time working (1-74 % actual employment rate) monthly-paid staff in primary care divided by all working monthly-paid staff in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Employees aged 34 or younger in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Employees aged 34 or younger in primary care divided by all employees in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Employees aged 35-54 in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Employees aged 35-54 in primary care divided by all employees in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Employees aged 55+ in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Employees aged 55 or older in primary care divided by all employees in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Foreign-born employees in primary care, balance ratio
kpi_description: Share of foreign-born people aged 18-64 among employees in primary care divided by the share of foreign-born people aged 18-64 in the county's population. The same share among primary care employees as in the county's population gives a balance ratio of 1. A value above 1 means a higher share of foreign-born people among employees than in the population, and a value below 1 a lower share. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Employees aged 55-64 in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Employees aged 55-64 in primary care divided by all employees in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Employees aged 65+ in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Employees aged 65 or older in primary care divided by all employees in the same area of activity, multiplied by 100 to show a percentage. Refers to region employees in November covered by the HÖK collective agreement. Source: SKR.

kpi_name: Doctor visits in primary care, own production (excl. maternal and child health clinics), per 1,000 inhabitants
kpi_description: Where applicable, includes clinic visits, day care visits (from 2008), home visits and home healthcare visits. A visit here means an outpatient visit: a care contact in outpatient care involving an in-person meeting between the patient and healthcare staff. Only outpatient visits documented in the patient's medical record are reported. Refers to production (visits made within the region, regardless of where the patient is registered as resident). Source: SKR and Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Doctor visits in primary care, other care providers (excl. maternal and child health clinics), per 1,000 inhabitants
kpi_description: Where applicable, includes clinic visits, day care visits (from 2008), home visits and home healthcare visits. A visit here means an outpatient visit: a care contact in outpatient care involving an in-person meeting between the patient and healthcare staff. Only outpatient visits documented in the patient's medical record are reported. Refers to production (visits made within the region, regardless of where the patient is registered as resident). Source: SKR and Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Visits other than doctor visits in primary care (excl. maternal and child health clinics), per 1,000 inhabitants
kpi_description: Where applicable, includes clinic visits, day care visits (from 2008), home visits and home healthcare visits. A visit here means an outpatient visit: a care contact in outpatient care involving an in-person meeting between the patient and healthcare staff. Only outpatient visits documented in the patient's medical record are reported. Refers to production (visits made within the region, regardless of where the patient is registered as resident). Source: SKR and Statistics Sweden (SCB).

kpi_name: Medical assessment within three days in primary care, share (%)
kpi_description: Shows the share of medical assessments in primary care carried out within three days of the decision that care should be given. The indicator covers medical assessments made in connection with visits, remote visits and home visits, and is one way of measuring access to care and treatment. A person who contacts primary care about a new or worsened health problem is entitled to a medical assessment within three days. The assessment must be made by licensed staff in primary care. Patients who were offered a visit but chose to wait longer, e.g. to see a particular care provider, are excluded from the calculation. The primary care mandate can vary between regions, which may affect the reported results. Waiting times may reflect ways of working adapted to the previous care guarantee. Changing ways of working takes time, which is important to consider when analysing and interpreting the results. The indicator is based on data reported monthly to the national waiting times database at the Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions (SKR). Source: Vården i siffror.

kpi_name: Telephone calls to primary care answered the same day, share (%)
kpi_description: Share of telephone calls to primary care answered the same day. Average of the year's twelve months. A new source is used from 2024, so comparisons with earlier years should be made with caution. The average of the monthly values is only calculated when data exist for at least 10 months. Source: Väntetider i vården.

kpi_name: Reasonable waiting time to a health centre, share (%)
kpi_description: Number of inhabitants in the region who fully or partly agree that waiting times for visits and treatment at health centres are reasonable, divided by the total number of respondents that year. Those who answered "Don't know" or did not answer are excluded. Source: Hälso- och sjukvårdsbarometern.

kpi_name: Trust in health centres, share (%)
kpi_description: Number of inhabitants who answered that they have high or very high trust in health centres, divided by the total number of respondents that year. Those who answered "Don't know" or did not answer are excluded. Refers to the patient's home region. Source: Hälso- och sjukvårdsbarometern.
